meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-14 | Start: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 48m | Location: Zoom | Hosts: Iris Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE) | Guests: Nina K., Samir P., Lena O. (PillarMed)
transcript:
[00:00] Iris Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. This is Iris from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Marco's joining from our SE team. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Nina Kapoor: Hi this is Nina K, Head of Platform at PillarMed.
[00:13] Samir Patel: Samir here, security.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Lena, ML eng. Good to meet you all.
[00:22] Marco Alvarez: Hey all, Marco. I'll be diving into the network/bench stuff.
[00:30] Iris Chen: Cool, agenda — clarify success criteria for the POC, workload sizing, network options (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink vs Private deployment), region/residency and egress constraints, and agree timelines.
[00:42] Nina Kapoor: Sounds good. We mainly want to validate that Redwood can run inference in our EU region, no data leaves EU, and that we can meet 99th p99 latency and cost targets. We'll also test private connectivity.
[00:55] Iris Chen: Great, can you state those targets numerically? p99 less than 300ms for 1k qps?
[01:03] Nina Kapoor: More like p99 < 350ms for 1k sustained qps for the smaller models, and for the 70B-ish model we expect higher but want predictable tail latency. Unit cost target: under $0.015 per 1k tokens — that's our long term. For the POC we accept some uplift.
[01:20] Samir Patel: And from security — data must not egress to US, key material in our KMS, audit logs retained, and we'll need evidence for SOC2 controls.
[01:30] Iris Chen: Understood. We'll scope Private deployment in EU-west-1 or use Redwood Private with VPC peering into your account — both can meet region restriction. Marco, maybe walk through connectivity options?
[01:41] Marco Alvarez: Yeah. So we have three typical patterns: 1) VPC peering — we peer a Redwood VPC into your VPC, traffic stays in-region, that's simple but requires route table updates and CIDR planning. 2) AWS PrivateLink — provides endpoint services so you never accept peering, it's single-AZ aware unless you front it with NLBs across AZs. 3) Full Private deployment (customer-managed) — we ship a Private control plane and inference runtime into your VPC or on-prem; that gives you full KMS integration and no cross-account peering but longer setup. Each has tradeoffs on egress, IAM, and operational ownership.
[02:25] Lena Ortiz: For us the easiest to approve is PrivateLink or in-account deployment. Our procurement doesn't like cross-account peering unless legal signs off.
[02:35] Samir Patel: Also we have strict egress restrictions — outbound only to a small allowlist: internal artifact store, our KMS endpoints, and a handful of CDN endpoints. Any metrics/telemetry that Redwood needs must be optional or routed via our proxy.
[02:51] Marco Alvarez: We can disable outbound telemetry by default and push logs to your S3 via cross-account role. For PrivateLink, telemetry can be delivered to an endpoint in your VPC. For peering, we can also mirror logs to your account. We'll highlight exact endpoints in the security packet.
[03:09] Iris Chen: Let's capture workload sizing now — Lena, can you describe the model mix and request shape?
[03:16] Lena Ortiz: Sure. Two groups: 1) Small conversational model ~7B used for user-facing chat at roughly 1k qps, avg token output 80, seq length 512. 2) Heavy context model ~70B for clinical summary and reranking — that's about 50 concurrent requests with long contexts up to 8k tokens, batched as async jobs (roughly 10k batch ops/day). The 70B will be quantized.
[03:46] Marco Alvarez: Helpful. So for the 7B model we can recommend an auto-scaling cluster with convolutional batching; expected p99 on Aurora-class GPU < 250ms given proper batching. For the 70B we need to size memory - likely 2x A100-equivalent or quantized M60-ish endpoints. We'll propose exact node types in benchmark plan.
[04:10] Nina Kapoor: Timeline — we want a 3-week POC: week 1 network and infra, week 2 run benchmarks and functional tests, week 3 iterate and produce report. Is that doable?
[04:20] Iris Chen: Yes, that matches what we've done for similar customers. 3 weeks is tight but doable if we get sample payloads and VPC details quickly.
[04:28] Samir Patel: I'll need to see the network design before we approve peering or PrivateLink — can you share a diagram with exact IP ranges and ports?
[04:36] Marco Alvarez: Absolutely. We'll include TCP/443, healthcheck ports, and specific IP ranges. For PrivateLink we'll show the ENI communication pattern and NLB setup.
[04:46] Nina Kapoor: Also need to confirm data at rest encryption and that KMS key usage logs are available to us.
[04:51] Iris Chen: Redwood Private supports using your KMS via external key policy; for hosted we use Redwood-managed KMS but can configure cross-account decrypt in Private. We'll put details in the packet.
[05:02] Lena Ortiz: Regarding benchmarks — what metrics will you produce? We need p50, p95, p99, token/sec, GPU utlization, memory pressure, and cost per 1k tokens. Also tail latency under cold-start scenarios.
[05:15] Marco Alvarez: We'll produce a benchmark spreadsheet: per-model throughput, latencies at different concurrency levels, resource utilization graphs, and an estimated cost model for each deployment type. We'll also include cold-start measurements for scale-up events.
[05:29] Iris Chen: For quantization — we'll test both int8 and 4-bit QK methods; Marco will recommend the quantization profile that preserves quality.
[05:36] Marco Alvarez: Note, some architectural caveats: KV cache warmup affects p99 heavily for autoregressive loads; we'll report steady-state vs warmup. Also prefix-caching is possible for chat but has residency implications if cache stored in a different account — we'll keep it inside your VPC for Private deployments.
[05:57] Samir Patel: On the topic of logs — we need audit logs for model calls, who invoked them, and obfuscation of PHI. Can Redwood redact at ingest or do we need to pre-process?
[06:08] Marco Alvarez: We provide hooks for server-side redaction and have integrations to run a redaction Lambda inside your account ahead of logging. For strict PHI policies customers often pre-process. We'll show a couple patterns.
[06:20] Nina Kapoor: Good. One more thing — region options. We want EU-only: either Ireland or Frankfurt. Which is better from Redwood's side?
[06:28] Marco Alvarez: We support both but availability of certain GPU SKUs can vary. For dedicated throughput in EU-FR, we might need cross-zone replication, but it's doable. We'll note the SKU differences in the benchmark doc.
[06:40] Iris Chen: OK let's run through a proposed success criteria list so we can all align. I'll read and you confirm: 1) POC runs in EU region with zero outbound to US. 2) p99 latency for chat model < 350ms at 1k qps. 3) 70B batch tasks complete within expected SLA (we'll define). 4) KMS integration and audit logs delivered to PillarMed. 5) Security sign-off on network architecture.
[06:59] Nina Kapoor: Those look good; can we add cost projection for month-1 at expected loads?
[07:05] Iris Chen: Yes we'll add cost projection. Marco will include cost delta between peering, PrivateLink, and Private deployment.
[07:12] Samir Patel: Our timeline dependency: legal needs time for cross-account peering approval; PrivateLink is usually faster, so we prefer that path if perf is acceptable.
[07:22] Marco Alvarez: Performance of PrivateLink is generally within a few ms of peering; the bigger delta is in multi-AZ failover patterns. We can run comparative lat tests during the POC.
[07:35] Lena Ortiz: For the batch rerank work — do you support async job ingestion via SQS or do we need a separate worker?
[07:43] Marco Alvarez: We support both. For POC we'll show a simple S3->Lambda->Invoke pattern but also can do direct job queueing. We'll provide example templates.
[07:54] Nina Kapoor: Ok if we get the security packet by Friday (04/16) and the benchmark plan Monday (04/20) we can start week of 04/27. That works for legal and infra.
[08:06] Iris Chen: We'll aim for that schedule. Now a few clarifying Qs for sizing — Lena, you mentioned 1k qps sustained: is that per region or global?
[08:15] Lena Ortiz: That's EU-only for chat. Global might be higher later but out of scope for this POC.
[08:22] Marco Alvarez: And tokenization — are your clients sending post-tokenized payloads or raw text?
[08:26] Lena Ortiz: Raw text. We also have pre-processing that adds a 300-token metadata prefix for clinical context — you'll see in sample payloads.
[08:34] Marco Alvarez: Good to know, that impacts sequence lengths. We'll include that in the bench harness.
[08:38] Samir Patel: A question on billing — we need invoicing to be in EUR and not USD, and a VAT note. Can Redwood support that for Dedicated/Private contracts?
[08:46] Iris Chen: Yes, for enterprise deals we can invoice in EUR. We'll loop in the finance rep in next email.
[08:52] Unknown: (mumble) so about TLS termination?
[08:55] Marco Alvarez: We recommend TLS terminate in your VPC for PrivateLink and Private deployments. For peering, TLS can terminate either side but certs are customer-managed for Private deployments.
[09:06] Nina Kapoor: Will you provide a minimal IAM role template so our infra people can pre-provision?
[09:10] Iris Chen: Yes, Marco will attach a minimal role and policy and a network diagram in the security pack.
[09:17] Marco Alvarez: Quick note on quotas — to simulate 1k qps we may need temporary quota bumps on our hosted infra if we go that route; for Private deployment quotas are customer-managed. We'll note required quota increases.
[09:29] Nina Kapoor: For acceptance criteria, can we include a simple functional test set — like 10 canonical prompts and 5 eval metrics?
[09:36] Lena Ortiz: We'll share a small eval set and scoring rubric.
[09:40] Iris Chen: Great. Let's talk deliverables: security pack (Iris) by 04/16, benchmark plan + node recommendations (Marco) by 04/17, sample payload + eval set (PillarMed) by 04/20, preliminary bench run in week of 04/27, wrap-up report week of 05/11. Any objections?
[09:57] Samir Patel: No objections. Make sure the pack includes ingress/egress ACLs and an options for telemetry suppression.
[10:05] Marco Alvarez: We'll include a telemetry suppression toggle and an architecture diagram for three connectivity options.
[10:12] Nina Kapoor: OK last question — do you support bringing-your-own-license for some of the model runtimes? We have some licensed model bits we can't expose.
[10:20] Marco Alvarez: We have an on-prem/private bundle that supports BYOL-like licensing, though we'd need legal review. We'll note it as an option.
[10:29] Iris Chen: Thanks everyone — quick recap and then we'll close. Recap: scope network options (prefer PrivateLink), run benchmarks for 7B chat and quantized 70B, deliver security pack + configs, and aim for POC start week 04/27. Action items and owners in follow-up email.
[10:46] Nina Kapoor: Thanks Iris, Marco, appreciate it.
[10:48] Lena Ortiz: Thanks.
[10:49] Samir Patel: Bye all.
[10:50] Iris Chen: Bye, we'll follow up with the packet.
[47:58] Transcript end (meeting length 48m). Note: there are a few small transcription errors above, names may be abbreviated.
